questions.stem: The functional role of a species in its habitat is called its
questions.explanation: A niche is the occupation of a species — what it eats, what eats it, when it is active and which resources it uses. Habitat is only the address; population, community and biosphere are counts of organisms at larger scales, not a role.

distractorRationale.a: A population is all the members of one species in an area, not their role
distractorRationale.c: A community is all the populations of different species living together
distractorRationale.d: The biosphere is the whole living layer of the Earth

questions.stem: Which of the following is an abiotic factor in a freshwater pond?

options.text: Competition between two species of tilapia

questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are non-living. The pH of the water is a chemical condition, so it is abiotic. Predation, competition and parasitism are all interactions between living organisms and are therefore biotic.

distractorRationale.a: Predation is a living interaction, so it is biotic
distractorRationale.d: Parasitism is a biotic factor

questions.stem: All the maize plants, grasshoppers, toads, snakes and soil bacteria living together in one farm plot constitute a
questions.explanation: A community is every population of every species in a given area, so plants, herbivores, carnivores and decomposers together make a community. It would become an ecosystem only if the non-living soil, water and climate were included in the description.

distractorRationale.a: A population is members of one species only, not maize plus animals plus bacteria
distractorRationale.c: A niche is a role, not a collection of organisms
distractorRationale.d: A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed

questions.stem: Pneumatophores in mangrove trees of the Niger Delta are an adaptation mainly for

options.text: obtaining oxygen from air because the mud is waterlogged
climbing towards light like a rainforest liana
storing water during the dry season

questions.explanation: Mangrove mud is saturated and contains almost no oxygen, so ordinary roots would suffocate. Pneumatophores grow up into the air and allow oxygen to diffuse down to the buried tissues. Salt management uses other features, such as salt glands, not the breathing roots.

distractorRationale.a: Salt is excluded or excreted by glands and membranes, not taken in by pneumatophores
distractorRationale.c: Lianas climb for light in rainforest; mangroves already stand in open light
distractorRationale.d: Water storage is a succulent adaptation of dry-land plants such as euphorbia

questions.stem: The relationship between Rhizobium bacteria in cowpea root nodules and the cowpea plant is an example of
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen into a form the plant can use, and the plant supplies the bacteria with carbohydrate and a protected niche. Both partners benefit, which is the definition of mutualism. An edaphic factor is a soil condition, not a relationship.

distractorRationale.a: Predation is hunting and eating another organism
distractorRationale.b: A parasite harms its host; Rhizobium benefits the cowpea
distractorRationale.d: Edaphic factors are non-living soil properties such as texture and mineral content

questions.stem: Savanna grasses in the Nigerian guinea zone recover quickly after a dry-season fire mainly because

options.text: their growing points (meristems) lie at the base of the shoot, protected in the soil

questions.explanation: Fire burns the aerial leaves, but the basal meristems and underground buds survive and send up new shoots when rain returns. That is why grazing and burning do not wipe savanna grass out. Pneumatophores and drip tips belong to mangrove and rainforest plants respectively.

distractorRationale.a: Pneumatophores are breathing roots of mangrove trees
distractorRationale.c: Grasses photosynthesise in daylight like other green plants
distractorRationale.d: Drip tips shed rain in rainforest leaves, not an adaptation to fire

questions.stem: A student lists rainfall, soil texture, a tapeworm in a goat, and wind as factors acting on a northern farm. How many of these are abiotic?
questions.explanation: Rainfall, soil texture (edaphic) and wind are non-living, so they are abiotic. The tapeworm is a living parasite, so that factor is biotic. Three of the four listed factors are therefore abiotic.

distractorRationale.a: Only counting one abiotic factor undercounts rainfall, soil and wind
distractorRationale.b: Two would be correct only if soil texture were wrongly treated as biotic
distractorRationale.d: The tapeworm is living, so it cannot be counted as abiotic

questions.stem: Which set of features correctly matches organism to Nigerian habitat?

options.text: Goat with broad browsing diet — Sudan savanna; euphorbia with succulent stem — dry north; mangrove with pneumatophores — Niger Delta
Camel with a hump — Cross River rainforest; cactus — mangrove swamp; tilapia with gills — Sudan savanna
Red colobus with a prehensile lifestyle — open Sahel; water lettuce with air tissue — desert dune; baobab with water-storing trunk — tidal mud
Drip-tip leaves — Sudan savanna; pneumatophores — Jos Plateau grassland; succulent stems — freshwater pond

questions.explanation: Goats thrive on coarse northern browse, succulent euphorbia stores water in arid compounds, and pneumatophores supply oxygen in Delta mud. Camels are not a Nigerian rainforest example, and drip tips, pneumatophores and succulence belong to rainforest, mangrove and dry land respectively.

distractorRationale.b: Camels are not rainforest animals in Nigeria; cactus does not grow in mangrove; tilapia are freshwater fish
distractorRationale.c: Colobus monkeys live in forest, water lettuce in freshwater, and baobab in savanna, not the habitats named
distractorRationale.d: Each feature is paired with the wrong habitat

questions.stem: In an ecosystem, the term 'niche' refers to

options.text: the physical location of an organism
the role and position a species has in its environment
the genetic makeup of a species
the food chain in which an organism is involved

questions.explanation: A niche encompasses the role an organism plays in its ecosystem, including its habitat, resource use, and interactions with other organisms. Understanding a species' niche is crucial for ecological studies and conservation efforts.

distractorRationale.a: This option confuses niche with habitat, which is only the physical environment.
distractorRationale.c: Genetic makeup refers to the genetic characteristics of a species, not its ecological role.
distractorRationale.d: While food chains are related, they do not fully define an organism's niche.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a biotic factor in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Biotic factors are living components of an ecosystem, which include plants, animals, fungi, and microorganisms. Fungi play a crucial role in nutrient cycling and ecosystem functioning.

distractorRationale.a: Temperature is an abiotic factor that influences the environment.
distractorRationale.b: Soil pH is also an abiotic factor affecting plant growth.
distractorRationale.d: Sunlight is an abiotic factor essential for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes a population?

options.text: All living organisms in a specific area
A group of different species living together
All individuals of a single species in a given area
The physical environment where organisms live

questions.explanation: A population refers specifically to all individuals of a single species that live in a designated area at the same time. This concept is fundamental in studying species interactions and ecosystem dynamics.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a community, not a population.
distractorRationale.b: A group of different species refers to a community.
distractorRationale.d: The physical environment is known as the habitat.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an abiotic factor that can affect an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Humidity is an abiotic factor that influences the moisture levels in the environment, affecting both plant and animal life. It plays a significant role in the overall health of an ecosystem.

distractorRationale.a: Predation is a biotic factor involving the interaction between species.
distractorRationale.b: Competition is a biotic factor that occurs between organisms for resources.
distractorRationale.d: Symbiosis is a biotic interaction between different species.

questions.stem: In ecology, the term 'habitat' refers to

options.text: the role of an organism in an ecosystem
the specific environment where an organism lives
the total number of organisms in an area

questions.explanation: A habitat is defined as the natural environment in which an organism resides, providing the necessary resources for its survival. Understanding habitats is essential for conservation and ecological studies.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a niche, not a habitat.
distractorRationale.c: Interactions between species describe a community, not a habitat.
distractorRationale.d: The total number of organisms refers to a population.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is most likely to influence the distribution of a species in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: The presence of predators is a significant biotic factor that can greatly influence where a species is found, as it affects survival and reproduction rates. Species often avoid areas where predators are abundant.

distractorRationale.a: Color may affect camouflage but is not a primary factor in distribution.
distractorRationale.c: Reproductive rate affects population dynamics but not directly the distribution.
distractorRationale.d: The age of an organism does not determine its distribution in the habitat.

questions.stem: Adaptations that help organisms survive in their environment are often a result of
questions.explanation: Natural selection is the process through which organisms better adapted to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring. This leads to the evolution of adaptations over time.

distractorRationale.b: Artificial selection is human-directed and does not primarily drive natural adaptations.
distractorRationale.c: Genetic engineering is a modern technique and not a natural process.
distractorRationale.d: While environmental changes can drive adaptations, the process of adaptation itself is through natural selection.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes an ecosystem?

options.text: A community of organisms and their physical environment
The total number of organisms in a habitat
The genetic diversity of a species

questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes both the living organisms (biotic factors) and the non-living components (abiotic factors) interacting in a specific area. This interaction is essential for energy flow and nutrient cycling.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a community but not the abiotic components.
distractorRationale.c: This refers to a population, not an ecosystem.
distractorRationale.d: Genetic diversity pertains to species-level characteristics, not ecosystem interactions.

provenance.note: Exam-pattern questions generated with OpenAI against the NERDC/WAEC/NECO/JAMB syllabus.

questions.stem: The concept of carrying capacity in an ecosystem refers to

options.text: the maximum population size an environment can sustain
the diversity of species in a habitat
the rate of energy flow in an ecosystem

questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the maximum number of individuals of a particular species that an environment can support indefinitely without degrading the habitat. It is influenced by resource availability and environmental conditions.

distractorRationale.b: Diversity of species relates to biodiversity, not carrying capacity.
distractorRationale.c: Resource availability influences carrying capacity but is not the definition.
distractorRationale.d: Energy flow is a different concept from carrying capacity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a primary producer in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Plants are considered primary producers because they convert sunlight into chemical energy through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain in ecosystems. They provide energy for herbivores and other consumers.

distractorRationale.a: Herbivores consume plants and are not producers.
distractorRationale.b: Carnivores are secondary or tertiary consumers, not producers.
distractorRationale.d: Decomposers break down organic matter but do not produce energy.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a community in ecology?

options.text: A single species of fish in a lake
All the trees in a forest
Various species of plants and animals in a savanna

questions.explanation: A community consists of different species living and interacting in a particular area. The savanna, with its diverse plant and animal species, exemplifies a rich ecological community.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a population, not a community.
distractorRationale.b: This refers to a single type of organism, not a community.
distractorRationale.d: Soil is an abiotic component and does not represent a community.

questions.stem: Which of the following best defines a niche in ecology?

options.text: The physical environment in which an organism lives
The role and position a species has in its environment
The total number of individuals in a species
The variety of species in a given area

questions.explanation: A niche refers to the specific role or function of a species within its ecosystem, including its habitat, resource use, and interactions with other organisms. It encompasses how a species meets its needs for food, shelter, and reproduction.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a habitat, not a niche.
distractorRationale.c: This refers to population size, which is different from a niche.
distractorRationale.d: This describes biodiversity rather than the specific role of a species.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of abiotic factors?

options.text: They are living components of an ecosystem
They include non-living elements like temperature and water
They do not influence living organisms

questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are the non-living components of an ecosystem that influence the environment and the organisms living in it. Examples include sunlight, temperature, water, and minerals.

distractorRationale.a: This describes biotic factors, not abiotic.
distractorRationale.c: Biotic interactions are not characteristics of abiotic factors.
distractorRationale.d: Abiotic factors significantly influence living organisms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of how organisms adapt to their habitat?

options.text: All organisms have the same reproductive strategies
Cacti have thick stems to store water in arid environments
Fish can survive in both freshwater and saltwater
Plants can grow in any type of soil

questions.explanation: Cacti have evolved thick stems to store water, which is a crucial adaptation for survival in arid environments. This adaptation allows them to thrive in conditions where water is scarce.

distractorRationale.a: Reproductive strategies vary among organisms depending on their habitat.
distractorRationale.c: Most fish are adapted to specific water types and cannot survive in both.
distractorRationale.d: Plants have specific soil preferences based on their adaptations.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors is primarily biotic?
questions.explanation: Predation is a biotic interaction where one organism (the predator) feeds on another organism (the prey). This interaction is essential in understanding population dynamics within an ecosystem.

distractorRationale.a: Soil pH is an abiotic factor.
distractorRationale.b: Sunlight is an abiotic factor that affects ecosystems.
distractorRationale.d: Temperature is also an abiotic factor.

The total number of species in an ecosystem

questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is defined as the maximum number of individuals of a particular species that an environment can support sustainably without degrading the habitat.

distractorRationale.b: This refers to biodiversity, not carrying capacity.
distractorRationale.c: Lifespan is unrelated to carrying capacity.
distractorRationale.d: Diversity of habitats is a different ecological concept.

questions.stem: The term 'community' in ecology refers to which of the following?

options.text: All the living organisms in a specific area
The physical environment of an ecosystem
All the different species that live together in a specific area
The interaction between living and non-living factors

questions.explanation: A community in ecology is defined as all the different species that live together in a specific area and interact with each other, forming a complex web of relationships.

distractorRationale.b: The physical environment describes the habitat, not the community.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes how abiotic factors can affect living organisms?

options.text: They have no effect on organisms
They determine the types of organisms that can survive in an area

questions.explanation: Abiotic factors such as temperature, water availability, and soil composition play a critical role in determining which organisms can survive and thrive in a given environment.

distractorRationale.a: This is incorrect; abiotic factors significantly influence organisms.
distractorRationale.c: Abiotic factors affect both plant and animal life.

distractorRationale.b: Plants are also living organisms and biotic factors.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between organisms and their environment?

options.text: Organisms do not adapt to their environment
Organisms can only survive in their natural habitats
Organisms interact with both biotic and abiotic factors in their environment

distractorRationale.b: While many organisms thrive in their natural habitats, some can adapt to new environments.

A group of animals living in a cave

questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes all living organisms (biotic factors) and their physical environment (abiotic factors) interacting as a system. A forest represents a diverse ecosystem with numerous interactions.

The physical place where an organism lives.

questions.explanation: A habitat is defined as the physical environment in which a species lives and thrives. It includes all the biotic and abiotic factors that affect the organism's survival.

distractorRationale.a: This describes a niche, not a habitat.
distractorRationale.c: This refers to community interactions, not the definition of habitat.

distractorRationale.a: Temperature is an abiotic factor that affects living organisms.
distractorRationale.b: Soil pH is an abiotic factor that influences the growth of plants.
